summary.text: A 29-year-old woman, ASA I, with nine years of secondary infertility and one prior successful pregnancy, no chronic illness, allergy or medications, and normal preoperative assessment and investigations was scheduled for diagnostic hysterolaparoscopy with chromopertubation under general anesthesia.

Under general anesthesia, laparoscopy showed flimsy uterine adhesions and beaded fallopian tubes. About 15 mg methylene blue was injected intrauterine; no dye spillage was observed, suggesting bilateral tubal occlusion. Three minutes after dye injection she developed unstable ventricular tachycardia with hypotension (72/40 mmHg), treated with a saline bolus, oxygen, phenylephrine, hydrocortisone and a norepinephrine infusion while cardioversion was prepared; the arrhythmia reverted spontaneously to sinus rhythm.

She was extubated and shifted to the postoperative ward on vasopressor support. After one hour she developed tachypnea with increased oxygen requirement and bilateral coarse crepitations; point-of-care ultrasound showed more than six B-lines with preserved cardiac function, and acute pulmonary edema was diagnosed.

Methylene blue cardiotoxicity was ruled out and methemoglobinemia was excluded (methemoglobin <0.1%, no bluish discoloration); fluid overload was considered less likely, and the authors described a potential anaphylactoid reaction. Serum tryptase was not measured.

Methylene blue cardiotoxicity and methemoglobinemia (methemoglobin <0.1%) were excluded; an allergic or anaphylactoid reaction to the dye was considered the most likely cause of the cardiovascular compromise and serum tryptase was not measured.
She was monitored in the ICU for 24 hours, shifted to the ward and discharged in good condition with advice for obstetrics outpatient follow-up for infertility management.

ambiguities.issue: The case text says point-of-care ultrasound showed more than six B-lines bilaterally and cites Figure 1; the Figure 1 caption says more than three B-lines in a single intercostal space. These describe different attributes (bilateral total vs one intercostal space) and are compatible, so both are kept as separate observations and no conflict is recorded.

evidence.quote: Point-of-care ultrasound demonstrated more than six B-lines (Figure 1) bilaterally
Lung ultrasonography demonstrating more than three B-lines (comet-tail artifacts) in a single intercostal space

ambiguities.must_not_infer: Do not reconcile the B-line counts or assume which lung zone the figure shows.

ambiguities.issue: The abstract says the dye test confirmed bilateral tubal blockage; the case text says no dye spillage was observed, suggesting bilateral tubal occlusion. This is a difference in hedging about the same observation, not two different findings; the case-text hedge is kept (provisional).

evidence.quote: confirming bilateral tubal blockage without dye spillage
No dye spillage was observed, suggesting bilateral tubal occlusion.

ambiguities.must_not_infer: Do not upgrade the tubal occlusion to a confirmed diagnosis.

ambiguities.issue: The abstract says the dye was administered transcervically and the case text says it was injected intrauterine. The wordings are compatible (path through the cervix, injection into the uterus) and are not a conflict; the route keeps the case-text wording.

evidence.quote: was administered transcervically
was injected intrauterine with resistance over three minutes

ambiguities.must_not_infer: Do not choose between the two wordings; the case text wording is kept as the route.

ambiguities.issue: The cause is stated as an allergic or anaphylactoid reaction (either/or) considered most likely; later wording is "potential anaphylactoid reaction". No test confirmed it and serum tryptase was not measured.

evidence.quote: an allergic or anaphylactoid reaction to the dye was considered the most likely cause of cardiovascular compromise
indicating a potential anaphylactoid reaction

ambiguities.must_not_infer: Do not record a confirmed allergic or anaphylactic diagnosis or a proven causal link to the dye.

ambiguities.issue: Preparation for cardioversion is described and the arrhythmia reverted before cardioversion was administered; the text does not state outright whether cardioversion was performed.

evidence.quote: with simultaneous preparation for cardioversion after a diagnosis of unstable VT was made
the arrhythmia spontaneously reverted to sinus rhythm before cardioversion was administered

ambiguities.must_not_infer: Do not record cardioversion as delivered.

evidence.quote: For future procedures in this patient, consideration of alternative dyes (e.g., indigo carmine, though also associated with risk) or saline infusion sonography may be appropriate.
